trust_decision.summary: The syslog sink decides which characters end a frame: every record-controlled string placed into the single RFC 5424 line (structured-data values and SD-NAME keys) must be neutralised so a log record cannot terminate or extend the frame; the decision is taken in escapeStructuredDataValue and formatStructuredData, reached from formatSyslogMessage only when includeStructuredData is enabled.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'structured data values containing C0 control characters', which points straight at escapeStructuredDataValue; the key-validation half sits five lines below in formatStructuredData:231-237.

fix_sites.module_kind: library sink formatter (internal helper of the published package)
library sink formatter (public sink's formatting path)

fix_sites.entry_point: getSyslogSink() via new internal isStructuredDataName() called from formatStructuredData()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the remaining fields are not record properties at all: MSG is free-form text whose framing belongs to the transport, and structuredDataId / appName / syslogHostname / processId are developer configuration, so the advisory's 'structured data values' wording is read as the whole protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Values that legitimately contain backslash, double quote and ']' must keep round-tripping through RFC 5424 escaping (asserted by the existing escaping test), non-string property values such as userId: 12345 must still be emitted as "12345" (documented example), and valid SD-NAMEs that are not [A-Za-z0-9_] (e.g. user-id, a.b) must still be included because keys are currently emitted verbatim; an over-broad fix that rewrites values, rejects anything non-word, or sanitises the whole line breaks all three.

O6_input_shapes: C0 control characters (\n, \r, \u0000, code points <= 0x1F) inside structured-data values, replaced by printable #NNN
SD-NAME keys containing a space, '=', '"', ']' or a control character (skipped)
SD-NAME keys longer than 32 characters (33-character key in the added test, skipped)
SD-NAME keys with non-ASCII code points (charCode > 126, skipped)
valid keys such as userId and method still emitted unchanged
property set where every key is invalid / empty property set -> structured data becomes '-'
values containing backslash, quote and ']' still escaped exactly as before

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Log message text (MSG field): record.message's even (template-string) elements are concatenated raw, so a message containing CR/LF starts a new syslog frame under LF framing.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: RFC 5424 MSG is free-form text; newline framing is a transport concern, and the advisory and its summary are worded about structured-data values.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function and file as the landing point (0 files, 0 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Structured-data ID: SyslogSinkOptions.structuredDataId is interpolated into [<id> ...] with no SD-NAME validation, although an RFC 5424 SD-ID has exactly the grammar the fix now enforces for property keys.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a developer-set sink option documented as 'Should follow the format', not attacker-controlled log data, so it is not covered by the advisory's property.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function and file as the landing point (0 files, 0 packages)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Syslog header fields: appName, syslogHostname (OS hostname by default) and processId are interpolated with no PRINTUSASCII/no-space validation, so a value with a space or control character shifts or forges header fields.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Header fields come from sink options and the OS hostname, i.e. trusted configuration outside the 'structured data' scope of the advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function and file as the landing point (0 files, 0 packages)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second frame formatter for a sibling transport/framing (RFC 6587 octet-counted, or a CEF/LEEF sink) duplicating formatSyslogMessage
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package already ships four connection classes (Deno/Node x UDP/TCP); a maintainer adding a new protocol would most naturally copy the formatter instead of routing through it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second structured-data emitter writing more than one SD element (RFC 5424 allows several) or an SD element built from implicit-context properties
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: formatStructuredData already takes the id as a parameter and its property loop is trivially copyable; multi-element structured data is the obvious next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Exporting formatSyslogMessage (or a lower-level send()) as public API so callers build frames without the sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The connection classes in syslog.ts are already exported and the package's public surface is one re-export line; exposing the formatter for custom transports is a natural request.
